title: Pulmonary TB in HIV — new HIV diagnosis, known HIV not on ART, or ART defaulter (child)
population: Paediatric < 15 y living with HIV and drug-susceptible PTB; excludes RR-TB, TBM / CNS / miliary TB, neonates < 4 weeks

admission.title: Diagnostic criteria — any one starts TB treatment

items.t: Xpert / culture positive on any sample, Rif susceptible
Urine LF-LAM positive (admitted child with HIV)
Symptoms + CXR suggestive, and/or TB contact

HIV: PCR if < 18 months; rapid if older (confirm)

admission.title: Severity — all children with HIV + TB = advanced HIV

items.t: Complicated CXR: airway compression, ≥ 1 lobe, cavities, miliary, complicated effusion
New HIV diagnosis, < 3 months on ART, or VL ≥ 1000 → NOT eligible for 4-month course: treat 6 months
On ART > 3 months, VL < 1000, non-severe: 4 months possible

TBM / CNS TB: ART after 4 weeks (REFER)

11. ADMIT → start TB treatment + CPT + pyridoxine; ART (boosted DTG) as soon as TB drugs tolerated, ideally ≤ 2 weeks

Creatinine / eGFR if on TDF · HBsAg · Hb

treatment.t: Intensive 2 months (daily): HRZ 50/75/150 dispersible + ethambutol 400 mg by weight band (box)
Continuation: HR 50/75 dispersible daily — non-severe 2 months, severe 4 months
Pyridoxine for ALL children with HIV + TB: < 5 y 12.5 mg, ≥ 5 y 25 mg daily
New HIV / < 3 months ART / VL ≥ 1000: 6 months (2 HRZE + 4 HR)
Cotrimoxazole — start / restart regardless of CD4 (TB = stage 3)
3–5.9 kg 2.5 mL · 6–13.9 kg 5 mL or ½ tab · 14–24.9 kg 10 mL or 1 tab · ≥ 25 kg 2 tabs daily
New / defaulted: start within 2 weeks once tolerating TB drugs
On ART: continue + boost DTG
Notify TB; record in RtHB, TB card, ART card
Rif resistant: STOP — REFER DR-TB
2–6 months with pneumonia: treat PJP too (LRTI child)
Counsel caregiver: TB + HIV together, adherence
Check all doses swallowed (DOT)
Siblings < 5 y / HIV+ exposed: TPT

tests.t: Baseline: CD4, Hb, HBsAg, eGFR if TDF

treatment.t: Start ART as soon as TB treatment is tolerated — ideally within 2 weeks
Re-initiate on a DTG regimen (disengaged children too)
ABC + 3TC + DTG (pALD dispersible / ALD) by weight — DTG boosted twice daily while on rifampicin
Doses by weight band: side 2 box
Fast-track initiation counselling; caregiver adherence plan

tests.t: VL; CD4 if VL not suppressed

treatment.t: Already on ART: continue; standard TB doses
On DTG / pALD / ALD: add boosted DTG dose 12 h later (weight band)
On EFV and suppressed: continue until 2 weeks after TB treatment, then DTG; unsuppressed → DTG now
On LPV/r: tablets double-dose; solution / pellets super-boost with ritonavir powder
ATV/r, DRV/r: not with rifampicin — expert / hotline
Infant on NVP prophylaxis or NVP-based ART < 3 kg / < 4 weeks: expert advice
Tolerating TB drugs: start ART now (boosted DTG)
Adjust TB and ART weight bands
Visual complaint: stop ethambutol, eye referral
Continue TB drugs and ART
Prednisone 2 mg/kg daily × 4 weeks (max 60 mg), taper over 2 weeks: airway compression, TB-IRIS
Severe / compression → REFER

tests.t: ALT + bilirubin; full LFT + INR if stopped

treatment.t: Symptomatic + ALT ≥ 100 or bilirubin ≥ 34 µmol/L (or asymptomatic ALT ≥ 200): STOP TB drugs, ART, cotrimoxazole
INR ≥ 1.5 → REFER as liver failure; 1.2–1.5 repeat 48–72 h
Symptomatic ALT 40–100, bilirubin < 34: continue, recheck 1–2-weekly
Rechallenge when ALT and bilirubin < 2 × ULN: R (or H) full dose → ALT at 2–3 days → add the other → ALT at 2–3 days; Z usually not rechallenged
Integrated TB + ART script and clinic date
Catch-up immunisations, vitamin A, deworming

items.t: Tolerating TB drugs, CPT (+ ART if started)
ART start date / boosting plan written
Integrated TB + HIV care at each visit (fewer visits, less LTFU)
Monthly × 2, then 2-monthly: symptoms, weight, adherence, weight bands
VL 3 months after ART start / re-engagement
Stop DTG boosting 2 weeks after rifampicin ends
Contacts: TPT for < 5 y and HIV+; test caregiver / siblings for HIV

appendix.title: Drug-resistant TB (RR / MDR / pre-XDR / XDR) — admission, tests and management

items.t: Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, TB-NAAT or culture reports rifampicin resistance
Child with TB disease and an RR-TB source case, or failing first-line treatment despite good adherence
Adults: never treat DR-TB without laboratory confirmation (molecular or phenotypic)
Children may be clinically diagnosed and still registered for RR-TB treatment
RR-TB: rifampicin resistant ± other drugs (includes MDR, pre-XDR, XDR)
XDR: RR + fluoroquinolone + bedaquiline or linezolid resistant
Isoniazid mono-resistant (Hr-TB): RHZE + levofloxacin ≥ 6 months — not this appendix

sections.title: Tests — send 'DR-TB reflex DST' on the RR result

items.t: Recall the patient; send a 2nd specimen for DR-TB reflex testing
Reflex = smear, culture, Xpert MTB/XDR (INH, ETO, injectables, FLQ) + phenotypic BDQ and LZD; genotypic ~48 h
FLQ, BDQ or LZD resistant: lab sends for pretomanid DST (NTBRL)
Extended DST (NICD) only on request: failing, BDQ / LZD resistance, prior 2nd-line exposure
No XDR result in 30 days: repeat sample, continue short regimen
Discordant results: phone the lab; treat the 'most resistant' scenario; PCAC / NCAC
≥ 2 good specimens for Xpert Ultra AND culture / DST; < 5 y gastric aspirate or induced sputum; stool Xpert (no culture); FNA of nodes
No own isolate: treat according to the source case's DST
Can attend clinic for review and DOT
Do not wait for smear / culture conversion to discharge
Airborne infection control; manage in a DR-TB unit / hospital
Not a registered DR-TB initiation site → link / REFER to the DR-TB unit for registration and start
Before start: register, counsel family, consent, psychosocial + substance-use + mental-health screen, contact tracing
Screen: severe EPTB (meningitis, pericarditis, osteoarticular, abdominal, disseminated / miliary)? documented BDQ / LZD / Pa / DLM resistance? pregnant?
None → BPaL-L for 6 months; start while awaiting DST and bloods
Any → long individualised regimen (WHO groups, page 2)
Hb < 8 g/dL: hospitalise; correct (transfusion) before BPaL-L
ANDH has no blood bank → REFER if transfusion needed
FLQ resistant → BPaL (stop levofloxacin) · INH / ETO / injectable resistance → continue BPaL-L
Extensive disease (bilateral cavitary, ≥ 3 lung zones) → extend to 9 months
> 1 month prior 2nd-line exposure is not a contraindication — exclude BDQ / LZD resistance
Resistance to BDQ, Pa, CFZ, DLM or LZD · culture positive at month 4 · BDQ / LZD / Pa stopped permanently for toxicity · clinical deterioration
Bedaquiline 200 mg daily × 8 weeks, then 100 mg daily
Linezolid 600 mg daily — at least 8 weeks; interruptions max 8 weeks in total
Levofloxacin 30–< 46 kg 750 mg · ≥ 46 kg 1000 mg daily (moxifloxacin 400 mg if unavailable)
6 months (extend to 9 at clinician's discretion); no pyridoxine needed

adult.t: LFX 30–< 46 kg 750 mg · ≥ 46 kg 1000 mg; MFX 400 mg (high dose up to 800 mg)

use.t: Include for CNS; omit if FLQ resistant

adult.t: Long regimen ≥ 30 kg: 400 mg daily × 2 weeks, then 200 mg Mon / Wed / Fri

use.t: Include if no resistance; reload after interruption (box)
All incl. CNS; Hb < 8, neutrophils < 0.75 or platelets < 50 → start / restart only in hospital

groups.step: Add one or both if possible
Add to complete the regimen when A / B cannot be used

use.t: Count as effective only if DST susceptible

adult.t: 30–< 46 kg 50 mg bd · ≥ 46 kg 100 mg bd

use.t: CNS; effective only if DST susceptible

adult.t: Imipenem 1 g bd (≥ 15 y) · meropenem 1 g tid or 2 g bd; amox/clav (125 mg clav) 30 min before each dose

use.t: CNS penetration; needs IV access → REFER
Only with documented susceptibility, audiometry, consent and TDM; never in pregnancy
CNS; only if no inhA mutation

long_regimen.t: ≥ 15 y not eligible for BPaL-L: individualised 18-month regimen (commonest reason: BDQ resistance)
As many group A drugs still susceptible + terizidone + clofazimine; add group C by likely efficacy, prior exposure, toxicity
CNS disease: drugs with CNS penetration; RR-TB meningitis include DLM, PZA and hdINH or ETO
Rescue (XDR): DLM (if unexposed), carbapenem + amox/clav, ETO (katG only), PAS, amikacin, MFX 800 mg; send EDST; NCAC

principles.t: ≥ 4 effective drugs; 5th if severe disease, CNS or ≤ 1 group A drug; all-oral
No pretomanid < 15 y (BPaL-L not for children)
Dose by weight band (Annexure 1, pp. 47–51); re-dose as weight changes
< 5 y, XDR, or BDQ / LZD / CFZ resistance → paediatric DR-TB expert / PCAC / NCAC
BDQ and DLM usually 6 months; LZD often tolerated only ~2 months — FBC 2-weekly first month then monthly

severe_def.t: Severe: bilateral CXR disease or cavities, airway-compressing nodes, EPTB other than peripheral nodes / simple effusion

rows.regimen: BDQ–LFX–CFZ–(TRD or DLM) 6 months ± LZD first 2 months

monitoring.t: Every visit: clinical review + adverse-event questionnaire; weight monthly
Smear + culture: baseline, 2 weeks, 4 weeks, then monthly
FBC / Hb 2-weekly to week 8, then 4-weekly (POC Hb acceptable)
Hb < 8 g/dL in weeks 2–8: admit; interrupt if symptomatic. Later: stop LZD if responding (after ≥ 2 months LZD)
Visual acuity (Snellen / tumbling E) every visit on LZD; > 2-line drop → ophthalmology, else stop LZD
Neuropathy: weeks 1–8 reduce dose / long regimen; weeks 8–16 reduce; ≥ 16 weeks stop LZD if culture converted
BDQ reload after interruption: < 2 wk none · 2–4 wk 400 mg × 3 d · 1–12 months 400 mg × 7 d · > 12 months 400 mg × 14 d (16–30 kg: 200 mg)
Grade ≥ 3 / serious AE: record and report on EDRWeb
After treatment: review + sputum smear / culture at 6 and 12 months

special.t: No BPaL-L: bedaquiline + delamanid + linezolid + levofloxacin for 6 months; no amikacin; ETO only if no alternative; notify NCAC; breastfeeding OK
TLD (ALD if < 30 kg or < 10 y); DTG is compatible with all RR-TB drugs; cotrimoxazole regardless of CD4
ART timing: after 2 weeks of DR-TB treatment once improving and tolerating; CNS TB: 4–8 weeks
Efavirenz contraindicated with bedaquiline; no zidovudine with linezolid
LFX 750–1000 mg 3 × / week · TRD 250 mg daily or 500 mg 3 × / week · EMB 15–25 mg/kg and PZA 25–35 mg/kg 3 × / week · stop amikacin · LZD, MFX, CFZ, Pa unchanged
Diabetes: tight glucose control; metformin ≤ 500 mg bd with DTG

consult.t: PCAC: complicated regimen choice, stopping LZD / BDQ / FQ / CFZ / DLM for toxicity, CNS RR-TB, discordant DST, children's regimens, rescue, end-of-life
NCAC (NCAC@witshealth.co.za): treatment failure, complicated children, FLQ-resistant CNS TB, XDR-TB (→ TB hospital), pregnancy notification
